contract.words: Make $12,000 within 45 days. I can put up to $2,500 of my own money in if it pays back inside that time. Any industry is fine.

terms.proofCondition: Owner money at risk (exposure) never exceeds $2,500 and must be paid back by settled cash inside the 45-day window; spending paid from buyer receipts is not owner capital

strategy.title: No plan yet: run a costed cold-email price-and-demand test for tax-season catch-up bookkeeping before committing the owner's money
strategy.why: All three discovered openings (catch-up bookkeeping, local-business website redesign, Shopify store build) rest on prices and demand the route author assumed. No buyer is shown paying these prices: the published bookkeeping list prices (Xendoo from $295/month of history; Bench includes catch-up free with a $1,910/yr plan) did not survive verification, and posted website-redesign requests on Freelancer.com draw average bids of $283-$656, far under a $1,500 offer. With no established price, current demand or close rate, no combination of the openings can be shown to carry $12,000 of settled cash in 45 days. Catch-up bookkeeping is the strongest candidate to test because the tax-filing deadline creates a dated reason to buy now and fulfilment can be subcontracted, so the test is run there first.

alternatives.why: Price $1,200 is an assumption; posted store-build jobs on Freelancer.com draw ~$390-$437 average bids, so buyers are not shown paying $1,200; no buying signal recorded.

alternatives.title: Bid on posted Freelancer.com / Fiverr web jobs directly
alternatives.why: Refused by Brain as a Brain-performed deliverable it has not proved; average bids of $25-$656 against 100-400 rival bids would need 30+ wins to reach $12,000.

PROOF by day 21: at least 3 paid $600 deposits and 3 written bookkeeper quotes at or under $600 per job -> plan the 10+ job build with the subcontractor. strategy.title: Conditional: tax-season catch-up bookkeeping sold by cold email at $1,200, fulfilled by a freelance bookkeeper - started only after a day-18 deposit test
strategy.why: Nothing is established yet (price, demand, close rate, fulfiller cost are all RECOMMENDATION), so the plan is a live test whose thresholds are set from the target backwards. Reading the target net of costs (the owner's money must pay back), each job nets about $543 after a ~$600 bookkeeper and Stripe fees, so 22 jobs are needed. Catch-up takes about 2 weeks (Bench: 2 weeks to 1 month), and a new Stripe account's first payout takes 7-14 days, so the last job must be sold by day 28 and delivered by day 42 for its final card payment to settle by day 44. The day-18 test (1,000 contacts, the Growth plan's upload cap) must therefore show at least 5 paid deposits - a 0.5% deposit rate, which on the 4,000 further contacts reachable on days 19-25 yields the remaining 17 - and 3 bookkeeper quotes at or under $600 with a 14-day turnaround. Below that pace 22 settled jobs by day 45 is not reachable and the plan stops. The $77 test spend is pre-proof owner money at risk: it is lost on STOP and is the owner's to approve inside his $2,500 ceiling; no further money is spent unless proof is met.

reviews.reasons: Correct that nothing is established: all three openings rest on RECOMMENDATION prices, no buying signal, no close rate and no fulfiller quote; the Xendoo/Bench list prices and Freelancer bids were rejected in verification (seller list prices and supplier-side bids are not what these buyers pay). Not proposing the website or Shopify openings as members is right. But the test as written does not hold together. (1) It uploads 1,500 contacts on the Instantly Growth plan, while its own source s5 (verified on instantly.ai/pricing: '$47/mo', '5000 Emails Monthly', '1000 Uploaded Contacts') caps uploads at 1,000; either the list is 1,000 or the cost is wrong. (2) The proof is not tied to the target. $12,000 at $1,200 needs 10 jobs settled by day 45 (more if the target is read net of the ~$600 bookkeeper cost). Proof is '3 paid $600 deposits by day 21', after which 7+ more jobs must still be sold, subcontracted, delivered (Bench quotes 2 weeks to 1 month for a catch-up) and settled through a new Stripe account whose first payout takes 7-14 days (s6) inside the remaining 24 days. The proof/stop thresholds must be the deposit count and dates from which 10 settled jobs by day 45 is still reachable, and stop when that pace is missed. (3) The contract allows owner money only if it pays back inside the window. The $77 is spent before proof and is lost on STOP, and the CONTINUE branch spends another $47; the plan must state that this spend is at risk and is the owner's to approve, or use a channel that costs nothing (e.g. the Craigslist route on the card) for the first measurement. Because the plan is a startable test with proof/stop/continue on unknowns only a live offer measures, it should be presented as CONDITIONAL with validation.decides = CURRENT_DEMAND, OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION (and FULFILMENT/ECONOMICS via the quotes), not as NO_PLAN.

strategy.title: Conditional: tax-season catch-up bookkeeping sold by cold email at $1,200, fulfilled by a freelance bookkeeper - started only after a day-18 deposit test
strategy.why: Nothing is established yet (price, demand, close rate, fulfiller cost are all RECOMMENDATION), so the plan is a live test whose thresholds are set from the target backwards. Reading the target net of costs (the owner's money must pay back), each job nets about $543 after a ~$600 bookkeeper and Stripe fees, so 22 jobs are needed. Catch-up takes about 2 weeks (Bench: 2 weeks to 1 month), and a new Stripe account's first payout takes 7-14 days, so the last job must be sold by day 28 and delivered by day 42 for its final card payment to settle by day 44. The day-18 test (1,000 contacts, the Growth plan's upload cap) must therefore show at least 5 paid deposits - a 0.5% deposit rate, which on the 4,000 further contacts reachable on days 19-25 yields the remaining 17 - and 3 bookkeeper quotes at or under $600 with a 14-day turnaround. Below that pace 22 settled jobs by day 45 is not reachable and the plan stops. The $77 test spend is pre-proof owner money at risk: it is lost on STOP and is the owner's to approve inside his $2,500 ceiling; no further money is spent unless proof is met.
